 Charlotte Airport Prepares for Thanksgiving Travel Surge and Storms
 Nov 21, 2026 • 20:00 
 • 0 Reads 
 Wulan Hapsari 
 Share 
 Font Size 
 A− 
 A 
 A+ 
 Bsinews.id, Jakarta , Charlotte Douglas International Airport is preparing for nearly 2 million passengers during the Thanksgiving holiday travel period, with officials warning of crowded roadways, increased security traffic and potential weather disruptions across major US flight routes. Airport projections released November 20 estimate 1.9 million passengers between Thursday and December 1.
 The expected passenger volume represents a 1.4% increase from last year. More than 9,300 departing flights are scheduled, up 2.6%, while American Airlines will operate over 8,300 departures, representing a 4% annual increase.

 Scroll To Continue with Content 
 American Airlines handles approximately 90% of air traffic at Charlotte Douglas. Nationwide, the carrier expects to transport more than 8 million customers across 85,000 flights during the holiday period, according to Joe Green, managing director of customer care for American Airlines at CLT.

 Green highlighted the scale of the airline's operations during the holiday rush.
 "To help put that in perspective, it will be an American Airlines flight departing every 13 seconds," said Joe Green, managing director of customer care for American Airlines at CLT.
 The busiest period at Charlotte Douglas is expected after Thanksgiving, particularly November 28, November 29 and November 30. American Airlines anticipates its highest departure volume on November 29, when nearly 700 flights are scheduled.

 Coastal Storm Threatens Eastern North Carolina as Boston Warms 
 Green warned that increased airport activity would also affect surrounding roads, particularly Wilkinson Boulevard and airport access routes.
 "With those numbers in mind, our message to travelers is simple: give yourself extra time and plan ahead," said Joe Green, managing director of customer care for American Airlines at CLT.
 The Transportation Security Administration expects more than 430,000 passengers to pass through Charlotte Douglas security checkpoints during the 13-day period, representing a 1.5% increase from last year. The agency plans to operate with full staffing capacity, according to Federal Security Director Jose Bonilla.
 Also Read 
 Heavy Rain and Strong Winds Threaten Georgia Coast 
 Bonilla explained that security preparations are designed to maintain passenger movement despite higher volumes.
 "We will have a full staffing capacity at our checkpoints to ensure that the travelers have a seamless travel experience through screening and on to their gates as early as possible," said Jose Bonilla, Federal Security Director for the TSA.
 He also identified November 29 as a particularly demanding day, noting that TSA screened more than 3 million passengers nationwide on the Sunday after Thanksgiving last year and expects an even higher figure this year.
 Also Read 
 Cold Front Brings Heavy Rain and Strong Winds to San Diego 
 Bonilla advised passengers to organize their luggage before arriving at security checkpoints, explaining that crowded bags frequently require additional inspections.
 "The more clutter that may be in a bag, most likely it will call for our officers to have to conduct a physical bag search," said Jose Bonilla, Federal Security Director for the TSA.
 Travelers must also comply with REAL ID requirements, which took effect in May 2025. Passengers without acceptable identification, including a REAL ID-compliant driver's license or passport, can use TSA's ConfirmID service, launched February 1, 2026, for a $45 identity verification fee.

 Additional airport services include touchless TSA PreCheck gates at Checkpoint 2, where facial recognition is matched with passport information in an airline application. Passengers requiring disability-related assistance can arrange support through their airline and TSA Cares.
 Parking availability is another consideration. Charlotte Douglas has 25,000 parking spaces, including 15,000 available for advance online reservations through ParkCLT.com or the CLT Airport app. Officials recommend reaching the parking facility at least 30 minutes before the intended terminal arrival time.
 Weather conditions could complicate travel even when storms remain outside the Charlotte region. Forecasts from the National Weather Service and other federal weather agencies identify several potential disruption periods between November 19 and December 1.
 Also Read 
 November 19 Forecast Brings Sunshine and Mild Weekend Weather 
 Heavy rain and possible flash flooding along Florida's east coast could affect flights serving Orlando, Miami and Tampa. Another coastal system may bring rain, flooding and strong winds from the Carolinas toward the Mid-Atlantic and Northeast, including New York and Boston.
 Additional disruptions could develop between November 23 and November 26, with heavy rain and strong winds affecting western coastal airports and mountain snow creating problems around Denver and Salt Lake City. A separate storm could bring thunderstorms to the Gulf Coast, Southeast and Charlotte area around Tuesday and Wednesday before Thanksgiving.
 Earlier National Weather Service forecasts also indicated a warming trend across Charlotte following a cold start to the week of November 16. Temperatures were expected to rise from approximately 59 degrees Monday to around 70 degrees Thursday and Friday, with minimal rainfall through much of the week.
 The November 16 forecast followed a Sunday high of 56 degrees and an early-morning low of 32 degrees. Both readings were below the November 15 seasonal averages of 63 and 40 degrees, respectively, according to the National Weather Service's Charlotte climate data.
 For the November 26 through December 1 return-travel period, forecasters are monitoring possible additional storms across the Gulf Coast, Mid-South and Southeast, alongside heavy mountain snow and strong winds in western states. The timing and severity of these systems remain uncertain.
